content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thigh prepared by rotisserie cooking with the skin left on is a juicy piece of meat with a crispy crust. The skin retains some fat, making the dish more flavorful and nutrient‑dense. It is often sold as a ready‑to‑eat product in supermarkets and restaurants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rotisserie cooking allows the meat to cook evenly while staying moist.
Chicken skin contains beneficial fatty acids but also adds extra calories.
Thighs are rich in protein and iron, making them a valuable nutrient source.
Traditionally the meat is cooked on a spit over an open flame, giving it a smoky aroma.
In some cultures chicken thighs with skin are considered a delicacy served on special occasions.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Iron from the meat helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels and energy.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune health and wound healing.

items.title: Skin supplies healthy fats
items.content: The skin contains monounsaturated fats that can be part of a balanced diet.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The skin adds significant calories and fat, so portion control is important.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Excess saturated fat intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Food‑borne bacteria risk
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can lead to salmonella or campylobacter contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken thigh with skin can be eaten hot, sliced into pieces, added to salads, sandwiches, or used in tacos. The skin can be eaten if crispy, or removed according to preference.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product in the refrigerator at 4 °C or below, in an airtight container, for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage freeze in a bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before consumption.
